# PR Review: #301353 — Move display-name, jsx-no-literals and react-perf rules to Oxlint

**PR:** [elastic/kibana#301353](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/301353) by @TamerlanG
**Created Date: 2026-11-10**

**Scale:** Small. It's mostly lint config plus mechanical code fixes. I skipped the flow trace because no runtime path changes in a meaningful way.

**Ownership (team: `@elastic/security-detection-engineering`)**
- **Your team's files (1):** `x-pack/solutions/security/plugins/lists/public/exceptions/components/builder/entry_renderer.tsx`. Your team also owns, in practice, the Lists and Security Solution rule blocks in `.eslintrc.js` and `.oxlint/*`; the config comments say they're "maintained and owned by the people within the security-detection-engine team".
- **Other teams' files:** `.eslintrc.js` (`@elastic/kibana-operations`); osquery and endpoint files (`@elastic/security-defend-workflows`); workflows files (`@elastic/workflows-eng`); resolver and flyout files (`@elastic/security-investigations`); attack discovery and entity analytics test (`@elastic/security-threat-hunting`); graph story (`@elastic/contextual-security-apps`); SIEM migrations header (`@elastic/automatic-migrations`)
- **Unowned:** `.oxlint/react.mts`, `.oxlint/team_overrides.mts`

Status: CI green (flaky but succeeded). 6 approvals so far (Operations, Investigations, Defend Workflows, Automatic Migrations, Workflows, Threat Hunting), none from detection engineering yet.

## Summary

Moves four React lint rules (`react/display-name`, `react/jsx-no-literals`, `react-perf/jsx-no-new-object-as-prop`, `react-perf/jsx-no-new-array-as-prop`) out of ESLint and into Oxlint's native versions. File scopes stay the same: Security Solution, Lists, Workflows and osquery. Oxlint's versions are a bit stricter and turned up 20 extra problems, which are fixed in code. The other 166 are all in Cases (`display-name` with `ignoreTranspilerName`), so Cases keeps running that rule in ESLint and turns it off in Oxlint. The description matches the diff. Linked context: [elastic/apps-dx#234](https://github.com/elastic/apps-dx/issues/234), follow-up to [#298182](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/298182).

## Files touched

- **Lint config** (`.eslintrc.js`, `.oxlint/react.mts`, `.oxlint/team_overrides.mts`): removes the rules from ESLint blocks and adds them to the matching Oxlint overrides. The ESLint `react-perf` plugin stays registered so existing `eslint-disable` comments still resolve. Cases gets an Oxlint `off` override plus a comment in ESLint explaining why it stays there.
- **`display-name` fixes** (resolver `styles.tsx` / `event_detail.tsx`, workflows `json_editor_common.tsx`, entity analytics test mock): adds `.displayName` to `memo(styled(...))`, `React.memo(() => ...)` and a `forwardRef` mock.
- **`jsx-no-literals` fixes** (8 Security Solution / workflows files, graph story): `&nbsp;` becomes `{'\u00a0'}`, which renders the same. The story's `TODO` becomes `{'TODO'}` and loses a misplaced disable comment.
- **`react-perf` fixes** (osquery ×5, `entry_renderer.tsx`): inline objects and arrays passed as props are hoisted to module scope or wrapped in `useMemo`.

## Assumptions

- Oxlint's `react/display-name` and `react/jsx-no-literals` with default options behave the same as eslint-plugin-react's defaults for everything outside Cases. The PR's evidence is "ESLint on main and Oxlint on this branch report the same diagnostics (none)", after the 20 fixes.
- Oxlint honours `eslint-disable` comments naming these rules. There are about 94 such comments for `display-name`/`jsx-no-literals` (79 files) and 21 for the two `react-perf` rules (14 files) in the affected areas. Nothing in the repo turns on unused-directive reporting, so ESLint won't start complaining about them either.
- `{'TODO'}` and `{'\u00a0'}` pass `jsx-no-literals` because `noStrings` is off by default, so only bare JSX text gets flagged.

## Risks

1. **Less feedback in the editor.** Anyone who only runs the ESLint extension won't see these four rules flagged while typing anymore. They'll only show up when Oxlint runs (pre-commit or CI). Same trade-off as the earlier Oxlint moves, so it's not new, but it does affect your team's daily workflow in Lists and Security Solution.
2. **Cases now depends on two linters for the same rule.** Oxlint applies `display-name` to Cases tests, server and common code, while ESLint applies the `ignoreTranspilerName` version to Cases `public` (non-test) code. Getting the `files`/`excludeFiles` globs right in both configs is what keeps them from overlapping or leaving a gap. They match today, but if someone edits one side later, the two can quietly drift apart.
3. **`entry_renderer.tsx` (your team): low risk.** `warningIconCss` moves from inside the `renderFieldInput` `useCallback` to a top-level `useMemo([sPaddingSize])`, and the callback's dependency list swaps `sPaddingSize` for `warningIconCss`. That's the same behaviour: the callback is still recreated only when the padding changes. `EMPTY_VALUES` is a shared module-level array, but I checked `AutocompleteFieldMatchAnyComponent` and it only reads or copies `selectedValue` (`uniq([...])`, `[...selectedValue, option]`) and never mutates it, so sharing it is safe.

## Open questions

- The Lists block for `display-name` / `jsx-no-literals` only matches `lists/public/*.{ts,tsx}` and `lists/common/*.{ts,tsx}`, which means top-level files only, with no `**`. That's carried over exactly from ESLint, so it isn't a regression, but it means almost all Lists components (like `exceptions/components/builder/*`) never ran these rules. Was it always meant to be top-level only, or is it an old glob bug your team might want to fix separately?
- Is there a tracking issue for Cases picking one of the three options (memo `displayName`, drop `ignoreTranspilerName`, or `@kbn/compat` via [#301273](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/301273))? Otherwise the "stays in ESLint" split could stick around for a long time.
- Changing the story's `TODO` to `{'TODO'}` is technically fine, but it works around the rule rather than fixing anything. Not a blocker since it's a story, but worth flagging as a pattern people shouldn't copy into real components.

## Notes for your codebase map

- Kibana is moving lint rules from ESLint to Oxlint one batch at a time. The usual pattern: delete the rule from `.eslintrc.js`, add it to the matching `.oxlint/*.mts` override, and leave the ESLint plugin registered so `eslint-disable` directives still resolve.
- `.oxlint/react.mts` has a shared `strictReactRules` map used by Security Solution, Workflows and Lists. Team-specific extras like `react-perf` live in `.oxlint/team_overrides.mts`.
- Oxlint globs don't support extglobs like `!(*.test)`, so ESLint's negative patterns become `files` plus `excludeFiles`.
- When the two linters' rule options can't be matched, the rule stays in ESLint for that scope and gets an `off` override in Oxlint. Cases `display-name` is the current example.
- Detection engineering owns the Security Solution and Lists lint rule blocks, according to the config comments, even though `.eslintrc.js` itself is owned by Operations.
